text:
andrew: FYI customer reported intermittent 502s from their prod service in VPC. App hosts show DNS failures to the internal service name, raising for triage.

infra-bot: Alert: support-ticket #34829 created (acme-corp). Initial severity: P2.

sana: Can you paste a quick repro (dig/curl) from a failing host? Also which VPC id and region?

andrew: From app host in us-east-1 (vpc-0a1b2c):
```
$ dig +short svc.prod.acme.internal
# <no output - empty, i.e. NXDOMAIN>
$ curl -sS -v http://svc.prod.acme.internal/health 2>&1 | head -n 6
* Could not resolve host: svc.prod.acme.internal
```

jeff: Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) private hosted zone association, 2) resolver rule overlap/forwarding. Run: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-0a1b2c --vpc-region us-east-1` and `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPCId,Values=vpc-0a1b2c`

andrew: Ran the hosted-zones-by-vpc call, output shows only Z98765 associated with vpc-0b2c3d (old VPC). vpc-0a1b2c is not in the list.
```
$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-0a1b2c --vpc-region us-east-1
{ "HostedZoneSummaries": [] }
```

sana: That matches the symptom — app hosts in prod VPC can't resolve because private zone isn't associated. Did the customer recently migrate or reprovision VPCs?

andrew: They migrated the cluster last week. Terraform apply ran during the cutover; suspect drift.

jeff: Two fixes: A) associate the private hosted zone back to prod VPC: `aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z1234567890 --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c` B) if there are resolver rules forwarding to another account, verify no higher-priority rule returning NXDOMAIN.

andrew: I performed the associate (with customer's permission):
```
$ aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z1234567890 --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c
{ "ChangeInfo": { "Id": "/change/C2EXAMPLE", "Status": "PENDING" } }
```

sana: Note: even after association, hosts may have cached NXDOMAIN. TTL is 300s on the zone. Recommend either flush local resolver cache or wait TTL. On Ubuntu systems: `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` or restart `dnsmasq`/`systemd-resolved` on app nodes.

andrew: Flushed caches on a couple of app nodes and retried:
```
$ dig +short svc.prod.acme.internal
10.10.5.42
$ curl -sS http://svc.prod.acme.internal/health
{"status":"ok"}
```

jeff: Also checked Route53 resolver rules — no overlapping forwarding rules for that domain. Looks clean. Leaving a note for infra: fix the Terraform module so future applies don't remove the association.

sana: I'll open a follow-up internal bug for the TF drift and tag infra. Also add a short runbook entry to check hosted-zone associations after migrations.

andrew: Customer confirmed their app health checks are green and 502s stopped. They saw resolution restored ~2m after association + cache flush.

infra-bot: support-ticket #34829 status -> resolved (reason: private-hosted-zone re-associated + cache flush).

jeff: Closing thread. If we see similar reports, check for private-zone association first (fastest triage). :thumbsup:
